questions.question:
**Directions: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement.**

Gitanjali __did not had__ school yesterday because it was a second Saturday.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"did not have"**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given underlined segment, the use of **the form of the verb** 'had' is **incorrect**.
 
• The verb '**had**' is the **past form** of 'have' and since '**did**' is the **past form** of 'do', **two past forms don't come together in a single sentence**.
 
• **When there is an auxiliary verb (here, did)**, the **main verb (here, had) does not need to be marked for tense**, because **the tense is shown in the auxiliary**.
 
• The verb that follows 'did' should be used in its base form.
 
• Therefore, the **base form of the verb 'had'** i.e. **'have' **should be **used here**.
 
• **Hence**, the correct answer is **option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence__: ***Gitanjali **did not have** school yesterday because it was a second Saturday.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

 
• However, in a **sentence** about the **past without an auxiliary verb**, the **main verb does need to be in the past tense form**.

questions.question:
**Directions: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement.**

The ﬁring of the missile __not only killed innocent persons and also__ created a political furore.

options.text: but killed innocent person and also
not only kill innocent persons and also
not only killed innocent persons but also

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"​not only killed innocent persons but also"**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the **use of the conjunction 'and'** is **incorrect**.
 
• The **conjunction 'and'** is used **to connect words of the same part of speech, clauses, or sentences, that are to be taken jointly**.
 
• The **conjunction 'but'** is used **to introduce a response expressing a feeling such as surprise or anger**.
 
• The construction "**not only...but (also)**" is called **correlative conjunction**. It is **used to present two related pieces of information**.
 
• **Both pieces of information are being presented as surprising or unexpected**, with the **second one being even more surprising than the first**.
 
• **Hence**, the correct answer is **option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence__: ***The ﬁring of the missile **not only killed innocent persons but also** created a political furore*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• ***Correlative conjunctions** are sort of like tag-team conjunctions. They come in pairs, and you have to use both of them in different places in a sentence to make them work. They get their name from the fact that they work together (co-) and relate one sentence element to another. **Correlative conjunctions** include pairs such as **"both/and", "either/or", "neither/nor", "not/but" and "not only/but also"**.*

questions.question:
**Directions: Identify the segment in the sentence, which contains the grammatical error.**

Yesterday I searched in every my cupboard for the shirt I couldn’t ﬁnd.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**in every my cupboard**".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the **singular noun 'cupboard'** is **incorrect** and thus the use of the determiner 'every' is also incorrect.
 
• The determiner 'every' refers to multiple numbers of people or items, but it considers these people or items as part of a similar collective group.
 
• '**Every**' can **only be followed by a plural noun when there is a number before that noun**.
 
• '**Each**' refers to a plural number of people or items, but it considers each person or item as an individual or dissimilar unit, it does not consider the group collectively.
 
• '**Each**' can be **followed by a determiner** (**my**, his, the, etc.) **and a plural noun**.
 
• The **format** is **Each of + determiner (here, my) + plural noun (here, cupboards)**.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

 

Correct Sentence__: *Yesterday I searched **in each of my cupboards** for the shirt I couldn’t ﬁnd*.

questions.question:
**Directions: Identify the segment in the sentence, which contains the grammatical error.**

Despite of her tiredness, Meera went into the kitchen to make some dinner for the children.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**Despite of her tiredness**".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the use of the preposition 'of' is incorrect or superfluous.
 
• The phrase "**despite of**" is **incorrect**, and **sounds distinctly non-native**.
 
• We can **confuse it with** "**in spite of**" which **basically has the same meaning** as '**despite**'.
 
• We should **use** only '**despite**' **instead of** "**despite of**".
 
• The word '**despite**' is **a preposition which takes a noun as its object**, and **doesn't require the preposition 'of'**.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is option 3.

 

Correct Sentence__: ***Despite her tiredness,** Meera went into the kitchen to make some dinner for the children*. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The word '**despite**' means **without being affected by; in spite of**.

questions.question:
**Directions: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order.**

A. Then he would give one leap, two leaps, through the snow, and sit up again on his hind legs and look all around.

B. A grey hare lived in the woods near a village.

C. Then he would prick up the other, jerk his whiskers, snuff, and sit up on his hind legs.

D. During the winter, when night came, he would prick up one ear and listen.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "BDCA".

​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence 'B' is independent of any other sentences as it is giving general information about "a grey hare". Hence, 'B' is the first part.
 
• The pronoun "he" in the sentence 'D' refers back to the 'grey hare' mentioned in the sentence 'B'. Hence, 'D' follows 'B'.
 
• The adverb "then" which means **after that** mentioned in the sentence 'C' is linked with the sentence 'D'. Hence, 'C' follows 'D'.
 
• The sentence 'A' is the concluding sentence. Hence, the sentence 'A' is the last sentence.

 

After rearranging the sentences__: *A grey hare lived in the woods near a village. During the winter, when night came, he would prick up one ear and listen. Then he would prick up the other, jerk his whiskers, snuff, and sit up on his hind legs. Then he would give one leap, two leaps, through the snow, and sit up again on his hind legs and look all around*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__** 

__
 
• Important Rules to Solve the Para Jumbles__:

 
 
• Read the sentences attentively and try to comprehend the idea or theme of the sentence and eliminate the irrelevant options.
 
• Try to identify the opening (independent sentence) and closing sentences (concluding sentence).
 
• Try to identify the mandatory pairs. Two sentences can be connected through various connectors and other determinants.

questions.question:
**Directions: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.**

Sujata shared the results of her experiment with her colleagues.

options.text: The results of her experiment are being shared with her colleagues by Sujata.
The results of her experiment were shared with her colleagues by Sujata.
The results of her experiment can be shared with her colleagues by Sujata.
Her colleagues shared the results of her experiment with Sujata.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**The results of her experiment were shared with her colleagues by Sujata**".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• In Active Voice, a sentence emphasizes the subject, performing an action.
 
• In Passive Voice, a sentence emphasizes the action or the object of the sentence.
 
• The given sentence is in the active voice and 'Sujata' is the subject and 'the results' is the object.
 
• When we convert this sentence into passive voice, the subject 'Sujata' of the active voice becomes the object, the object 'the **results**' **becomes** the **subject**.
 
• The passive format "were + V3" should be used.
 
• This is the active and passive voice rule for the past simple tense.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is option 2.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Verbs of passive format have a different set of tenses (*V3 - Past participle or Third form of the Verb) as given below in the table:

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 TENSE
 ACTIVE
 PASSIVE
 PASSIVE CONVERSION

questions.question:
**Directions: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order.**

**A:** According to the EPR, the corporation expects such manufacturers to develop a collect back system for plastic waste.

**B:** The Municipal Corporation has introduced the extended producer's responsibility (EPR) for producers and generators of plastic waste.

**C: **The producers are persons engaged in the manufacture, or import of carrying bags, multilayered packaging and sheets, and persons using them.

**D: **They must formulate a plan to collect re-usable waste generated from their products within a prescribed timeframe.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "BCAD".

​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence 'B' is independent of any other sentences as it is giving general information about the "Municipal Corporation". Hence, 'B' is the first part.
 
• The noun "producers" in the sentence 'C' refers back to the 'producers' mentioned in the sentence 'B'. Hence, 'C' follows 'B'.
 
• The noun "manufacturers" mentioned in the sentence 'A' refers back to the phrase "**persons engaged in the manufacture**" in the sentence 'C'. Hence, 'A' follows 'C'.
 
• The sentence 'D' is the concluding sentence. Hence, the sentence 'D' is the last sentence.

 

After rearranging the sentences__: *The Municipal Corporation has introduced the extended producer's responsibility (EPR) for producers and generators of plastic waste. The producers are persons engaged in the manufacture, or import of carrying bags, multilayered packaging and sheets, and persons using them. According to the EPR, the corporation expects such manufacturers to develop a collect back system for plastic waste. They must formulate a plan to collect re-usable waste generated from their products within a prescribed timeframe.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__** 

__
 
• Important Rules to Solve the Para Jumbles__:

 
 
• Read the sentences attentively and try to comprehend the idea or theme of the sentence and eliminate the irrelevant options.
 
• Try to identify the opening (independent sentence) and closing sentences (concluding sentence).
 
• Try to identify the mandatory pairs. Two sentences can be connected through various connectors and other determinants.
